sections.content: Hungarian number words from nulla to tíz are used as basic personal-information building blocks — learn them as ten fresh vocabulary items rather than a system to reason out. Use hány? to ask for a number or quantity; the context tells you what's being asked.
sections.title: Numbers and asking for one

sections.content: Two numbers that trip people up: hat (six) and hét (seven) look and sound almost identical — say them side by side a few times until your ear can tell them apart. hány? is the all-purpose 'how many / what number' word, and doesn't change shape depending on what's being counted — Hány éves vagy? literally asks 'how many years are you.'
